html:
The foundation of the Data Cloud Consultant certification: what Data Cloud (now Data 360) is, how it relates to the rest of the Salesforce Platform, the data lifecycle from ingestion to activation, and the organisational building blocks (data spaces, objects, entitlements) you will configure in every implementation.

Naming note (verified, Spring '26): On October 14, 2025 Salesforce rebranded Data Cloud → Data 360, and the certification "Salesforce Certified Data Cloud Consultant" became Salesforce Certified Data 360 Consultant (exam code Data-Con-101). The product, exam guide, and this course use the current name; you will still see "Data Cloud" in older docs and repos (including the folder naming of this project). Treat them as the same platform.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Explain what a customer data platform (CDP) is and which problems Data 360 solves.
  • Describe the single end-to-end data lifecycle: ingest → harmonize → unify → segment/insight → activate.
  • Distinguish data spaces, data sources, data streams, data lake objects, data model objects, and unified profiles.
  • Explain how Data 360 relates to the CRM (Salesforce core), Marketing Cloud, Tableau/CRM Analytics, and Agentforce.
  • Summarise the licence/add-on model and the personas who configure Data 360.
  • Locate the lab's service classes, flows, and objects that model this architecture.

1. What Data Cloud Actually Is

Salesforce Data 360 is a hyperscale customer data platform (CDP) that runs natively inside the Salesforce Platform. Unlike the transactional CRM, Data 360 is built to store huge volumes of customer data from any source—not just Salesforce objects—in a shared, open architecture, and then to act on that data across every Salesforce cloud.

The core value proposition is a unified, governed, real-time customer view ("Customer 360") that is:

  1. Connected — pulls data from CRM, ERP, e-commerce, POS, web, mobile, marketing, third-party data lakes, and streaming events.
  2. Harmonized — maps every source's shape into a shared canonical data model.
  3. Unified — uses identity resolution to link records about the same real-world individual/account.
  4. Actionable — segmentation, calculated insights, activation targets, and AI grounding turn unified profiles into business actions.

Why it exists: the C360 problem

Salesforce has always stored customer data in many places: Account/Contact in the CRM, data extensions in Marketing Cloud, Case/Entitlement in Service Cloud, plus your company's data in warehouses and lakes. Each system holds a siloed, partial view of the customer. A CDP consolidates those silos into a single, real-time customer record that every cloud can consume.

QuestionCRM aloneCRM + Data 360
"Who is this order history for?"Only what exists in SalesforcePOS + e-commerce + loyalty + CRM unified
"Is this person a churn risk?"Limited to CRM fieldsCalculated insight over all sources in real time
"Can my marketing journey use the service case volume?"ManualSegment membership activates to Marketing Cloud
"What can my Agentforce agent know about this customer?"CRM records onlyFull unified profile via data graphs

2. The End-to-End Lifecycle

Every Data 360 initiative follows the same five-stage pipeline. The certification tests your ability to map a business requirement onto the correct stage and its configuration.

text
  +-----------+   +-----------+   +-----------+   +-------------+   +-----------+
  | INGEST    |-->| HARMONIZE |-->| UNIFY     |-->| INSIGHT &   |-->| ACTIVATE  |
  | streams   |   | DLO -> DMO|   | identity  |   | SEGMENT     |   | to the    |
  | (API/batch|   | mapping   |   | resolution|   | calculated  |   | ecosystem,|
  | /CRM conn)|   | transforms|   | rulesets  |   | insights    |   | actions,  |
  +-----------+   +-----------+   +-----------+   +-------------+   | agents    |
                                                                     +-----------+
  1. Ingest — bring source data in as data streams (Salesforce CRM connector, Ingestion API, batch loaders, streaming, cloud-storage connectors, MuleSoft).
  2. Harmonize — raw data lands in Data Lake Objects (DLOs), then is mapped and transformed into Data Model Objects (DMOs) in the canonical Customer 360 data model.
  3. Unify — identity resolution rulesets (exact + fuzzy matching) merge records that point to the same real-world customer into a Unified Individual (and company into Unified Account).
  4. Insight & Segment — SQL-based calculated insights (KPIs like lifetime value or churn score), segments that filter unified profiles, and data actions.
  5. Activate — publish segments/attributes to activation targets (Marketing Cloud, Advertising, Salesforce CRM, webhooks, Data Cloud-triggered flows) and ground Agentforce agents in the unified profile.

3. The Organisational Model

Data 360 lives in the same org you already know, but adds its own configuration layer. The building blocks you must know cold:

ConceptAnalogyDetails
Data spaceA storage container / partitionOrganisational unit that isolates data (and its metadata) — e.g. one data space per business unit, brand, or use case. Data is not shared across data spaces by default.
Data sourceA system you connectCRM (Salesforce), Marketing Cloud, cloud storage (Amazon S3, Azure Blob, Google Cloud Storage), external connectors, MuleSoft, the Ingestion API.
Data streamA configured pipeline from a sourceOne stream = one Subject Area; each stream creates a Data Lake Object (DLO) with an append/upsert refresh schedule.
Data Lake Object (DLO)The raw landing zoneStores ingested data in raw (often lz-append or upsert) form, one DLO per stream, e.g. POS_Sales__dlm.
Data Model Object (DMO)The normalised canonical objectThe harmonized shape, e.g. Individual__dlm, ContactPointEmail__dlm, UnifiedIndividual__dlm. DLO fields map into DMO fields.
Unified profileThe resolved customer recordThe UnifiedIndividual linked to every matched source record; the object marketing, service, and agents consume.
Calculated insightA SQL-derived KPI objectSELECT aggregations over DMOs (e.g. total spend, days-since-last-purchase, churn score).
SegmentA saved audience definitionFilters over unified profiles/calculated insights; membership can be static, on-schedule, or real-time.
ActivationThe published audienceSends segment members + selected attributes to a target (Marketing Cloud data extension, ad platform, Salesforce object, webhook).

Data spaces

A data space is the logical container for a complete Data 360 implementation. Every resource (stream, DLO, DMO, unified profile, segment, activation) belongs to exactly one data space. Choose a data space per:

  • Business unit — a bank running retail + commercial units keeps them isolated.
  • Data sensitivity — regulated data (finance/health) quarantined from marketing data.
  • Use case — a customer-success view vs. a marketing view, each with its own governance.

Data spaces matter for Agentforce too: a data space is how you carve out the slice of the identity graph an agent may see (verified: Salesforce's own Help Agent graph exposes a filtered data-space view to the customer-success agent, isolating it from the broader marketing identity matrix).

4. Relation to the Rest of the Platform

Data 360 is the data layer of "Agentforce 360": it unifies data that every consuming layer depends on, and it is the mechanism behind RAG indexing/chunking, Agent Analytics, and Digital Wallet.

LayerHow Data 360 powers it
CRM (Sales force/Service Cloud)Data Cloud-triggered flows, related lists, unified-profile enrichment of Case/Lead/Account, Data Cloud data in Lightning.
Marketing Cloud EngagementSegments activate into data extensions; journeys are fed by segment membership.
Advertising / Sales journeysSegment activation to Google, Meta, LinkedIn, etc.
Tableau / CRM AnalyticsDMO and unified-profile data available for dashboards without ETL.
AgentforceData graphs, retrievers, prompt-template merge fields, Apex actions, and RAG all ground agents in unified, governed customer data.
MuleSoft / APIsIngestion API, Query API (/services/data/vXX/query), and data actions expose Data 360 programmatically.

Licences vs. add-ons (exam-style)

  • Data 360 licence — grants the platform, a data space, standard CRM connectors, a base data volume, and core features.
  • Entitlements / add-ons — additional data volumes, Marketing Cloud activation connectors, advertising activations, real-time/streaming ingestion, zero-copy (BYOL), and so on. The exam asks you to match a requirement (e.g. "ingest 2 TB","real-time web events") to the add-on rather than the base licence.
  • Permission sets — the personas: Data 360 Admin, Data 360 Marketing Admin, Data 360 Marketing Viewer, and delegated admin groups. Setup access lives in the Data 360 tab in Setup.

5. This Lab's Mirror of the Architecture

This repository cannot provision a real Data 360 org from source control (Data 360 configuration is org-level and largely not source-format), so the force-app/ lab models the Apex/automation surface around Data 360 with CRM-side objects and services that mirror the pipeline:

Lifecycle stageLab artifact (force-app)What it teaches
IngestDataCloudIngestionService + Data_Stream_Log__cThe pattern of an ingestion API/loader facade, payload validation, dedupe by external key
Harmonize/TransformCalculatedInsightServiceMaterialising KPI rows the way a calculated insight SELECT would
UnifyIdentityResolutionHelperServiceExact vs. fuzzy match scoring, merge-candidate scoring (a toy version of a ruleset)
SegmentSegmentMembershipServiceComputing and persisting segment membership sets
ActivateActivationSyncService + Activation_Audit__cBuilding activation payloads, retrying, and auditing a publish
Consent/govConsentManagementService + Consent_Preference__cConsent capture and consent-gated activation
Real-timeDataActionHandlerService + Data_Action_Event__ePlatform-event-driven data actions
AnalyticsDataCloudReportingServiceBuilding and reading dashboards/reports on the CRM side

You will meet each class again in the phase where the concept belongs; CaseTriggerHandlerService wires enrichment into Case so you can see a full "unified profile → service context" story.

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Map a business requirement to a stage

For each requirement, name the pipeline stage (ingest / harmonize / unify / insight / activate / govern):

  1. "Pull 3 years of POS transactions from the data warehouse into a data space."
  2. "Put store_id, customer_id, total into a canonical Individual-shaped object."
  3. "Link POS customers and CRM contacts who are the same person."
  4. "Compute average order value per customer."
  5. "Publish high-value customers to a Marketing Cloud journey."

Then reverse it: pick one of the four capstone use cases in Phase 17 and draw its lifecycle on paper.

Exercise 2: Read the lab services

Open force-app/main/default/classes/DataCloudIngestionService.cls and ActivationSyncService.cls. Identify the mirror of each lifecycle stage and write down the single method that represents it. Run the deploy smoke test:

text
sf org create scratch -f config/project-scratch-def.json -a dc
sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app
sf apex run test -c

Exercise 3: Data-space decision

You are a consultant for a retailer that runs three brands and stores customer financial data. Propose a data-space split (how many, and why), and state what would change if one brand needed to share high-value customers with the others (answer: a shared activation/data-action crossing spaces or a governed cross-space sharing rule — not a merged space).

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
Data 360 (Data Cloud)Salesforce's hyperscale CDP; ingests, harmonizes, unifies, segments, and activates customer data on the Salesforce Platform.
Data spaceAn organisational data container isolating data and metadata for a business unit or use case.
Data streamConfigured pipeline from a source; creates a Data Lake Object.
DLOData Lake Object — raw landing zone for ingested data, one per stream.
DMOData Model Object — the harmonised/normalised canonical object (e.g. Individual).
Unified profileThe resolved customer record (Unified Individual) after identity resolution.
Calculated insightA SQL-defined KPI or metric over DMOs.
SegmentA saved audience/filter over unified profiles or insights.
ActivationPublishing a segment and its attributes to an external or internal target.
Zero-copyIngesting/referencing data in external lakes without copying (BYOL).
CDPCustomer Data Platform — software that manages unified, persistent customer profiles from multiple data sources.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can name the five pipeline stages in order and give one configuration for each.
  • I can explain the difference between a DLO and a DMO, and where each sits in the pipeline.
  • I can describe what a unified profile is and which process creates it.
  • I can decide when to create a new data space vs. reuse an existing one.
  • I can explain the Data Cloud → Data 360 renaming and the current certification name (Data 360 Consultant, Data-Con-101).
  • I know the Data 360 permission-set personas (Admin, Marketing Admin, Marketing Viewer).
  • I can point to the lab service classes that mirror ingest → activate in force-app/.
